item.evidence: frontend/src/components/WorldGlobe.jsx:14 defines VA: 0.02 and AD: 0.12; :95 accepts a missing polygon only when Math.hypot(p.lat - at.lat, p.lng - at.lng) < TINY_R[p.code], otherwise :97 opens the large polygon's code. backend/countries_data.py:47 gives VA's reference point as 41.9,12.45. backend/data/countries50.geojson:1 contains VA's western boundary at 12.427539,41.900732, while frontend/public/countries.geojson:1 contains Italy but no VA polygon. MiMundo.jsx:72 passes the reference list into places and :57-59 opens the selected code's panel.
item.expected: R-025: "clicking directly on a tiny country such as Gibraltar or Vaticano at close zoom opens that country's own information panel ... not ... the larger country around it". The identity of the clicked rendered region must determine its panel across that region, not only near an approximate reference point.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source calculation predicts a click at latitude 41.901, longitude 12.428, inside the rendered Vatican polygon, reaches Italy's click polygon but misses the Vatican override: sqrt(0.001² + 0.022²) = 0.02202 degrees, greater than 0.02. Parts of Andorra and Monaco similarly extend past their radii. Travellers clicking the displayed country therefore get the neighbour's name, flag and visit action. They can recover by searching the country picker; no runtime click was executed.
reproduction_steps: Open Mi Mundo and zoom closely to Ciudad del Vaticano.
Click inside the western part of its rendered boundary, around 41.901 latitude, 12.428 longitude.
The source predicts the Italia panel rather than Ciudad del Vaticano; use the country picker to access Vaticano instead.
item.surface: Mi Mundo globe, close-zoom country clicks
item.title: Parts of tiny countries open the surrounding country's panel — picking uses a too-small circle instead of the rendered border

item.evidence: AddCityDialog.jsx:41 first posts /cities, :42 subsequently uploads the selected files, and :47 catches either failure without storing r.data.city.id or refreshing/closing the dialog; every retry executes :41 again. backend/server.py:505-507 inserts a new UUID city before returning; :641-643 saves photos individually; :609-610 rejects unsupported formats and :617 can fail at external storage. AddCityDialog.jsx:90 accepts image/*, which includes formats outside server.py:588's allowlist.
item.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls and server-side operation identity preserve one create/send/charge/booking per intent"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Walk failure boundaries for batches and preserve prior valid work". Retrying the same city after a photo error should continue that city's upload or clearly expose its partial success, not create another visit.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that selecting a city and an unsupported image (for example an SVG file offered by the image/* picker), or encountering an external upload failure, commits the city but leaves the user in the form with an error. Removing the rejected file and pressing Guardar ciudad posts a new city rather than attaching to the first one. The traveller acquires duplicate visits (and potentially duplicate partially uploaded photos), affecting visit frequency and globe labels; they must find and manually reconcile/delete the extra records. This is recoverable but the advertised retry is not safe.
reproduction_steps: Choose Añadir ciudad, select Roma and enter a visit date.
Select an SVG image in Fotografías (or encounter an upload-provider failure) and press Guardar ciudad.
After the error, remove the rejected file and press Guardar ciudad again.
Open the cities list: source predicts two Roma visits for this single save intent.
item.surface: Añadir ciudad → Fotografías → Guardar ciudad; POST /api/cities followed by POST /api/photos
item.title: A failed photo upload makes retrying a new city create another visit — the dialog forgets that the city was already saved

item.evidence: backend/server.py:655 defaults limit to 200, :663 uses to_list(limit) with no offset or cursor; PhotoGallery.jsx:39 requests /photos?city_id=... or trip_id=... without a limit/pagination and :96 maps only that response. server.py:469-472 counts all city files, so CityDetail.jsx:76 can announce more files than can be opened. Shared city/trip endpoints likewise stop at 500 (server.py:818,833), and Shared.jsx:19-24 has no pagination.
item.expected: request: "Quiero poder subir tantas fotografías como quiera" and "Visualizar las fotografías en cuadrícula", "Eliminar fotografías", "Editar descripciones"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Check pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". Every stored gallery file must remain accessible, with bounded requests and a way to reach subsequent files.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after a traveller uploads 201 gallery files in supported batches, all remain stored and the city header counts 201, but the city gallery only renders the first 200 and offers no next page or load-more control. The same limit affects trip galleries; shared galleries silently truncate at 500. The traveller cannot inspect, edit, reorder or delete omitted files through the gallery. Their original files are not proven lost; ordinary use requires removing visible files or keeping galleries artificially small to reach them.
reproduction_steps: Add a city and upload 201 supported images in batches of 50 or fewer.
Reload that city's page and compare the Galería file count with the rendered grid.
Try to reach image 201: no pagination/load-more action exists.
Share a city with over 500 images; the shared page similarly omits the remainder.
item.surface: City/trip Galería and public share galleries
item.title: Large city galleries hide stored photos with no way to browse them — the UI fetches only the first 200 records

item.evidence: backend/stats.py:65 defines unique_cities as {(c['name'].strip().lower(), c['country_code']) for c in cities}; :103 and :112 return that set's size. backend/server.py:267-269 similarly groups country city counts with $addToSet of only $toLower '$name'. In contrast, server.py:246-247 returns each search result's name, coordinates and admin1, and :503-507 stores these distinguishing fields; WorldGlobe.jsx:51 displays every located record. MiMundo.jsx:23 renders the reduced cities_visited count and :115 renders cities_count.
item.expected: request: "Número de ciudades visitadas" and "Buscador mundial de ciudades"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record ... identity ... a distinct similar item ... must remain separate". Distinct geographic cities selected from search must count separately even when their display names and country match. For Springfield, Illinois and Springfield, Massachusetts, the distinct places total is 1 + 1 = 2; repeated visits to the same Springfield may still count as one city.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: source predicts that visiting two homonymous cities in the same country counts as only one city, because their stored coordinates/admin1 are discarded for identity. A traveller can save two different Springfields and see two correctly positioned locations on the globe but only one city in world/personal statistics and country counts. City-based achievements are also delayed. Both records remain available, but the traveller cannot obtain an accurate total without falsely renaming one city.
reproduction_steps: Use Añadir ciudad to search Springfield and select the Illinois, United States result; save it.
Search again and save Springfield, Massachusetts, United States with its different coordinates.
Open Mi Mundo and Mis estadísticas: the source predicts one unique city rather than two; the globe and records retain both locations.
item.surface: Mi Mundo cities statistic, Mis países city counts, Mis estadísticas and city achievements
item.title: Travellers visiting same-named cities get understated totals — city identity discards location and region

item.evidence: server.py:536-541 changes the city's trip and moves its photos' trip_id, but :548 updates only the city; it never clears old trip cover_photo_id values. enrich_trip at :362-366 trusts the stored cover id without checking current membership. TripDetail.jsx:39 and public Shared.jsx:68 use this cover_url. PhotoGallery.jsx:118 allows an image from a city's trip gallery to be selected as cover through PUT /trips/{id}; CityEditDialog.jsx:36-39 offers the destination-trip selector. server.py:703-710 authorizes the moved photo using its current trip/city/public-profile status, not its former trip's cover reference.
item.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Propagate ... changes to lists, detail pages ... and other views"; request: trips have their own cover photograph and cities are organized inside their corresponding trips. After moving a city and its photos, the original trip's cover must be cleared or replaced with a remaining photo instead of pointing at a photo now belonging elsewhere.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that moving a city to another trip leaves its photo selected as the previous trip's cover. The owner still sees a cover from a city no longer in that trip, including after reload. For a private owner sharing the old trip only, the old share page's image then fails authorization because the photo belongs to the unshared destination trip. The user must notice and manually choose a replacement cover; moving the city did not keep the two trip presentations consistent.
reproduction_steps: Create trips A and B under a private profile; add a city with an image to A.
In A's gallery, choose that city's image as A's cover and share trip A.
Edit the city and change Viaje from A to B; save.
Reload A: it still uses the moved image. Open A's share link signed out while B and the city are unshared: that cover is no longer authorized.
item.surface: City Editar → Viaje selector; old trip detail/card/shared cover
item.title: Moving a city leaves the old trip with an unrelated or broken cover — photo reassignment does not clear cover references

item.evidence: backend/server.py:641 processes only files[:50] and :644 returns an ordinary success list without rejected/skipped-file metadata. AddCityDialog.jsx:90 permits arbitrary multiple selection, :91 displays all files.length, :42 submits all, and :43 reports the city saved without comparing upload counts. PhotoGallery.jsx:79 likewise has unrestricted multiple selection; :51-53 reports only the returned upload count, not that selected files were discarded.
item.expected: request: "Quiero poder subir tantas fotografías como quiera" and "Subir varias fotografías simultáneamente"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "visible rejected/skipped input" and "a ... batch applying half its entries must not report complete success". Either upload the complete selected batch, chunk it, or explicitly reject/explain the per-request limit before accepting a partial batch.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: selecting 51 valid photos causes the server to save just 50, silently ignoring the last photo. In the add-city flow the user is told the city is saved and the dialog closes although its displayed 51-file selection was not fulfilled. The omitted original is not proven deleted, but the traveller has an incomplete gallery and must discover the missing file and upload it separately. This is an ingress defect, separate from the later gallery pagination limit.
reproduction_steps: Open Añadir ciudad and select a searched city.
Choose 51 valid JPEG images in Fotografías; observe the form's 51-file selection count.
Save, then inspect the city photo count or upload response: source predicts only 50 stored files and no skipped-file warning.
item.title: Travellers' photo selections are silently incomplete — upload processing drops every file after the first 50

item.evidence: backend/server.py:53 specifies the unique (user_id, country_code) index and :948-950 awaits its creation on startup. create_visited :295 first checks for a record, then :297 inserts via add_visited :280-282 without catching DuplicateKeyError. The only DuplicateKeyError suppression in this file is in the separate city-created-country path (:509-512). AddCountryDialog.jsx:33 calls this endpoint and :42 displays errMsg, whose fallback in lib/api.js:11-15 is a generic failure.
item.expected: R-033: "two identical visits ... submitted at the same time leave one stored record and the second submission is refused"; checklist, code-quality: "Runtime paths avoid tracebacks, unhandled 5xx". With a functioning unique index, the duplicate should be a handled conflict explaining that the country was already saved.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: two concurrent save requests for GI can both pass the pre-check; the store correctly allows one insert but the other raises an uncaught DuplicateKeyError, producing a 500 instead of the endpoint's normal 409. A traveller saving from two tabs sees an unexplained failure although their visit was stored. No duplicate/data loss is predicted with the index present; refreshing the page is an inexpensive recovery, so this is minor rather than a failed essential save.
reproduction_steps: Open Añadir país visitado for Gibraltar in two signed-in tabs before it is visited.
Save in both closely enough that both pre-checks precede insertion.
The source predicts one saved visit and one unhandled 500/generic error, rather than an explained already-registered conflict.
item.title: A concurrent country save shows a generic server error despite succeeding once — unique-index conflicts are not handled

item.evidence: server.py:69-75 catches every create_indexes exception, logs it and continues; :948-950 merely awaits that non-failing helper and then permits startup. The required visit uniqueness exists only in INDEXES at :53; create_visited :295-297 and create_city :509-511 use separate read-before-insert operations rather than an atomic upsert/guard when the index is absent. compute_stats in backend/stats.py:59 deduplicates sovereign counts but server.py:288-289 returns every stored visit and :737-741 produces a stamp per stored visit.
item.expected: R-033: "On startup the backend ensures the unique indexes it relies on ... two identical visits ... leave one stored record"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "A check before insert alone races". If a required uniqueness index cannot be established on a new database, the app must not begin accepting writes that depend on that missing guarantee.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: on a fresh database, if creation of user_country fails (for example a transient database error during startup, followed by normal write availability), the backend still starts with no unique visit index. Two concurrent saves can then both pass the existing-record check and both insert GI. The traveller receives duplicate country-list entries and passport stamps; removing the country deletes only one row, so the visit can appear to return on refresh. Statistics deduplicate sovereign codes, so an inflated world percentage is not claimed. Repairing the missing database guarantee requires operational intervention; users can only clean up individual duplicates.
reproduction_steps: Deploy against a new database with no visited_countries user_country index, and encounter an index-creation failure during startup while subsequent normal reads/writes become available.
Sign in and submit Gibraltar visits concurrently from two tabs before either request inserts.
Both requests can succeed because startup tolerated the missing index.
Reload Mis países or Mi pasaporte; source predicts duplicate GI entries/stamps, with one still present after one delete.
item.surface: Backend startup; concurrent country/city visit creation; Mis países and Mi pasaporte
item.title: Travellers can acquire duplicate visits after index provisioning fails — startup logs uniqueness failures and accepts writes anyway

item.evidence: AddCityDialog.jsx:41 posts /cities, :42 subsequently uploads files, and :47 catches failure without retaining r.data.city.id or refreshing/closing; retry executes :41 again. TripDialog.jsx:32-35 similarly creates the trip before uploading its cover but never retains the new id for retry. AddCountryDialog.jsx:33-36 creates the visit before uploading its photo; its catch at :42 leaves the dialog in creation mode. backend/server.py:399 and :507 insert new UUID trip/city records each time, while :295-296 refuses the already-created country with 409. All three pickers accept image/*, including formats outside server.py:588's allowlist; :609-610 rejects those files and :617 can fail at external storage.
item.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls and server-side operation identity preserve one create/send/charge/booking per intent"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Walk failure boundaries for batches and preserve prior valid work". Retrying after a photo error should continue the existing saved object, or clearly communicate partial success and provide recovery, not repeat creation.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that a rejected image or upload-service failure occurs after the city, trip or country has committed, but all three forms remain open showing only an error. Retrying creates duplicate cities/trips; for countries it now fails with 'Ya tienes este país registrado' and never reaches the corrected photo upload. Travellers must discover the partial record, close the form and edit it (or manually delete duplicates). Partially uploaded city images may also be repeated. Original local images are not proven lost, but ordinary retry is unsafe and the advertised combined save does not complete cleanly.
reproduction_steps: Choose Añadir ciudad, select Roma, enter a visit date and select an SVG image (or encounter an upload-provider failure).
Press Guardar ciudad; after the upload error remove the rejected file and save again: source predicts two Roma visit records.
The same sequence in Nuevo viaje with a failed cover creates duplicate trips.
In Añadir país visitado, let the photo upload fail after saving Gibraltar; replace the photo and retry: creation now returns Ya tienes este país registrado instead of uploading it.
item.surface: Añadir ciudad, Nuevo viaje and Añadir país visitado, with photos/covers
item.title: Retrying a photo-failed save duplicates travel records or blocks recovery — forms restart creation after the record already committed

item.evidence: backend/stats.py:89 starts country_counter with one entry per city record, :90-91 then adds every trip's country_codes, and :94-96 selects the maximum as most_visited_country. Cities store trip_id (server.py:449,503-507), but the calculation does not use it to avoid counting the trip and its component cities as separate country visits. frontend/src/pages/Stats.jsx:52-54 labels the result 'País más visitado' without disclosing a cities-plus-trips score.
item.expected: request: "País más visitado"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Establish overlapping/excluded groups ... aggregation order". Inference from that label: cities visited during one explicitly linked country trip are not additional trips to that country. For one Italy trip with four Italian cities versus two France trips with one French city each, country-visit frequency is Italy 1 and France 2, so France is most visited.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: source predicts an Italy score of 1 trip + 4 cities = 5 and a France score of 2 trips + 2 cities = 4, declaring Italy 'País más visitado' even though the user visited Italy once and France twice. Adding cities to a single trip can change the reported most-visited country without another country visit. Travellers receive an incorrect personal statistic; their underlying history remains available, but they cannot correct this output while accurately keeping all cities.
reproduction_steps: Create one completed Italy trip and add Roma, Florencia, Venecia and Milán to that trip.
Create two completed France trips on different dates, each with a Paris visit linked to its respective trip.
Open Mis estadísticas and inspect País más visitado.
The source predicts Italia (score 5) rather than Francia (two distinct trips; implementation score 4).
item.surface: Mis estadísticas → País más visitado; GET /api/stats
item.title: The most-visited country can be the one visited fewer times — the statistic adds cities and their parent trips together
